_why: Role track for PART PROGRAMMING, the fourth pack authored under docs/profiling/role-pack-authoring-guide.md and one of the last two roles of Batch 1. fam_machining stays the generic machining interview bound at ISCO unit 7223; fam_cam_programming binds the NCO programming occupation directly (job_domain specificity 50 beats unit 40), so a part programmer gets programming depth and every other machining worker is untouched.
_scope: PART PROGRAMMING IN GENERAL, NOT DESK-CAM-ONLY -- owner ruling of this session. NCO 7223.6003 'CNC Programmer' defines the occupation as producing the component program 'using manual data input or by use of a remote computer', which is one trade with two work surfaces: the man at a CAM seat and the man typing the program into the controller at the machine. Binding only a desk-CAM reading of the role would have left every MDI programmer on fam_machining's six generic questions. That ruling is what makes programming_mode the FIRST item rather than the experience gate: it is this pack's disambiguator, exactly as machine_type is qp_machining's, and every row below reads honestly for both surfaces because each carries an escape chip.
_first_question: programming_mode is is_core AND is_mandatory and sits at display_order 0, so selectItem serves it before the tier gate -- mandatory items are found first, in display_order. Two mandatory items is a deliberate divergence from the turner/miller/grinder shape: the CAM-versus-MDI split decides how every later answer should be read, so an unanswered split is a fail-closed condition, not a missing nice-to-have. ask-budget.guard.test.ts charges one retry per mandatory item, so this pack costs 14 items + 2 retries + qp_universal's 8 + 2 = 26 of MAX_ENGINE_ASKS 28 -- the same worst case as qp_cnc_turning.
_depth: THE TIER GATE IS programming_experience, asked SECOND, immediately after the split. It cannot be experience_years from qp_universal: phase order runs occupation_specific BEFORE universal_tail, so the universal answer does not exist yet when these items are selected. Its options carry value_number ONLY. pack-registry.service.ts resolves valueText ?? valueNumber ?? valueBool, so adding a value_text would make the answer a STRING; every gte below would then compare a string to a number, compare() returns null, and the predicate is false forever. A permanently-false ask_if is a question that is never asked, silently -- the #776 defect that sat in qp_welding for the life of the pack.
_budget: MAX_ENGINE_ASKS is 28 and qp_universal spends 8. Tier 0 is 7 items (15 total), tier 1 adds 2 (17), tier 2 adds 2 (19). This pack is SMALLER than its siblings on purpose: the ratified sheet prints NINE capability rows, CAPABILITY_ROW_BUDGET is 9, and this pack asks exactly the nine questions those rows need plus the split and the gate. Padding to the turner's fifteen would buy attributes that nothing renders. The three fresher items are gated on programming_experience <= 0 and a senior never sees them; a fresher skips tiers 1 and 2 entirely, so his worst case is 15 + 3 = 18. The tiers are mutually exclusive by construction, which is why the fresher branch costs the senior nothing.
_sheet: SECTION B IS READ OFF THE RATIFIED REFERENCE SHEET (Nitin Deshmukh, CAM Programmer -- Programmer, 7 yrs), not invented. Its section title is 'Software, machines programmed & capability' and its nine rows are CAM software, Machines programmed, Controllers posted, Programming work, CAD model handling, Post-processors, Simulation, Drawings and Sector worked. Every row has exactly one question here that fills it, and there is no question here that no row needs. Post-processors and Simulation are BANDED single-selects rather than free text: the sheet prints a capability sentence ('Edits and tests post-processors', 'Vericut and in-CAM collision check before release'), which is a band, and a banded chip keeps a low-literacy worker tapping instead of typing while avoiding the answer_type 'number' path that has no Flutter widget. A 7-year programmer clears both tier gates, so the reference sheet's nine rows are all reachable for exactly the worker it was written from -- which is the parity check.
_shared_attribute_names: controller_brand, drawing_reading, sector_worked, iti_workshop_machines, trade_test_status and iti_project_work are attribute names and served strings this pack takes VERBATIM from qp_cnc_turning / qp_vmc_milling / qp_cnc_grinding. Verbatim matters twice over. Each divergent string is a Devanagari TTS twin that has to be authored and rendered forever -- aligning qp_cnc_grinding's shared items to the turner and miller wording cut its twins from 50 to 13 -- and a shared attribute NAME lets a matcher looking for Fanuc find this worker under the same key as a turner or a miller. controller_brand keeps its sibling wording even though the sheet row is titled 'Controllers posted', because the fact is the same fact: which controller sits on the machine this program runs on. The printed English is the resume map's job, not the chip's.
_fresher: Guideline section 11 #1: a fresher's Zone 4 is training, trade test, machines used in the workshop and project work, and the History heading never renders empty. These three items are the ask half; resume-fresher-rows.ts, fed by this role's descriptor, is the render half, and its fresher.workshopMachines is keyed by the STORED VALUE of iti_workshop_machines -- which is why the option values here match the sibling packs character for character.
review_note: Drafted for owner review (Prakash). The chip vocabulary in this pack is DRAFTED AND NOT YET RATIFIED -- neither the CAM software list, the machine and controller lists, nor the programming-work, post-processor and simulation ladders have been corrected by a practising part programmer. Same open redline as qp_cnc_turning, qp_vmc_milling and qp_cnc_grinding; see docs/registers/trade-content-ratification.md.

items._why: THE DISAMBIGUATOR, and the load-bearing item of the pack. fam_cam_programming is scoped as part programming in general, so this splits the desk CAM programmer from the man doing manual data input at the controller before a single capability question is asked. Modelled on qp_machining's machine_type, which settles the occupation inside a family retrieval has already pinned. The escape chip exists because a worker can be routed here by an alias and still not be the one who writes the program -- 'Program koi aur banata hai' is a real answer, and a pack that could not record it would be inventing one.

NO DIGITS IN AN option_key -- slugKey enforces ^[a-z_]+$ at runtime and a key like vmc_3_axis makes the whole pack unparseable, so the axis count is spelled out in the key and printed in the label. why_text is the sibling packs' machine-question line, verbatim.

items._why: TIER 2. Sheet row 'Post-processors' -- prints 'Edits and tests post-processors'. A BANDED single_select, not free text and not answer_type 'number': the sheet's string is a capability level, and a band is what a low-literacy worker can tap. Gated at five years because editing and proving a post is the senior half of the ladder Junior Programmer -> Programmer -> Senior Programmer.
items.prompt_text: Post-processor ke saath aap kitna kaam karte hain?
